protocol.scope: Each group has one WorldCore and A/B projects, one writer, explicit interleaving; no model or trained policy
protocol.worker_inputs: Opaque ports expose only tools/observe/call; requirements, routes, exact work IDs, policy targets, expressions and bytes are discovered publicly
protocol.actions: Finite adopt/update, request/wait, exact read, JSON create/write and submit, with at most one action per scheduler step
protocol.alternative_paths: Several currently owned works and several ports round-robin; worker builds one combined JSON, while P3 independently accepts two-file layout
protocol.controller_events: Availability changes after actual A blocked/B completed outcome; formal requirement revision after real initial completion; a deliberate authorized pause after observation before first adoption creates an actual rejected tool call
protocol.pre_freeze_supplement: published_successor adds a separate release-to-obligation-to-public-worker closed loop after the original six-group 55-check development protocol; earlier development reports do not cover this supplement
protocol.checkpoint_boundary: Explicit completed step-result checkpoint, JSON roundtrip of public progress/transcript only; not arbitrary process crash or exactly-once policy recovery
protocol.comparison: Compare original captured definitions/observations/action args/returns to worker transcript; inspect exact work/submission/binding and immutable bytes separately after execution. Replacement updates the old submission's current_applicability projection to superseded_requirements; every other submission field, including approval/answer/versions/adoption snapshot, is compared unchanged. Unrelated works are compared in full.
limitations: Transparent finite program; no general planning claim
P4 arithmetic is a declared scalar sum, not finance-quality evaluation
Paused-tool rejection is a deliberate environment failure probe, not a spontaneous production failure
No API/GPU/training or new crash cuts in P4

omissions: Original port captures retain all actual returned tool definitions, observations and tool responses. Their byte hashes are retained and worker transcript equality is checked per group. Large repeated observation/definition payloads are not copied here; the full actual tool-call entries, scalar submitted JSON, protocol/checks and public policy outcome/checkpoint references are preserved. Observation summaries are direct extracts from saved historical returns, never reconstructed from final world state.
boundaries: Explicit completed-step public policy checkpoint only; not arbitrary crash recovery.
Missing-route policy waiting, real world blocking, action-budget truncation and actual paused-tool rejection remain separate outcomes.
The automatically published successor group is the distinct 12-check supplement to the six original groups with 55 checks.
No model/API/GPU/training result; finite transparent scheduling and declared calculations.
